caption: The drawing depicts a mechanical object resembling an old-fashioned iron lock or fastening device. The primary component shown in the central part of the image includes two vertical, black metal arms with pointed prongs at the tops and several rivets or bolts along their length, each arm curving outward at the bottom. Between the arms is a symmetrical scrollwork design, also rendered in dark tones, with a pair of circular, gear-like elements—one on each side—near the upper center. A central vertical bar descends from the top scrollwork, ending in a simple latch or hook, and is fixed with visible rivets. Beneath this assembly is a horizontal bar or beam rendered with stippling and shading to emphasize its iron texture, complete with rivets and two vertical supports. Above the primary image, two smaller insets provide a front and a side view of the same lock or mechanism, drawn with lighter lines and including proportional guides. The overall composition is monochromatic, executed in shades of gray and black, on a beige or light tan paper background delineated by a simple rectangular border. A faint signature appears in the lower left corner.
title: Pa. German Hinges and Hasp on a Conestoga Wagon Tool Box
